messages:
anya: Heads-up — support escalation: customer on dedicated-prod-usw2 reporting sudden p99 spikes and intermittent timeouts since our host kernel rollout last night. They see p95 ~200ms -> 700ms and p99 jumping to 1.8s.

carlos: Which rollout window? any correlating infra events?

anya: Rollout started ~2026-03-14T03:10Z. Metrics link: https://grafana.redwood/shot/uuids/abc123 (customer-provided). They attached traces showing long kernel io wait and sporadic nvme latencies.

linda: I pulled node logs from their fleet node-011. dmesg: multiple "nvme nvme0: completion timeout" around the same spike. iostat shows nvme util hitting 99% with qdepth surge.

kevin: Repro steps I ran on our repro rig: start load against r19-encoder with concurrent 180 clients using `wrk` then watch p99 with our probe. Command: ```wrk -t12 -c180 -d120s http://localhost:8080/v1/generate``` reproducible 20/20 runs after we applied the kernel package.

anya: Interesting — we also pushed a GPU driver update (451.67 -> 453.10) in the same window for the Dedicated pool. Could be a stacking issue: driver+kernel causing heavy host DMA or pagecache writeback patterns.

carlos: I grepped host vmstats during spike — dirty pages burst then fsyncs from local checkpointers. `/proc/vmstat` shows high pgmajfault spikes, and `vm.dirty_ratio` is still at 20.

linda: Quick mitigation applied on node-011: reduced dirty_bytes and disabled merges on nvme: ```echo 16777216 > /proc/sys/vm/dirty_bytes; echo 1 > /sys/block/nvme0/queue/nomerges; echo none > /sys/block/nvme0/queue/scheduler``` Immediately p99 fell from ~1.8s -> ~420ms for in-flight requests. Not ideal long-term but buys time. :white_check_mark:

kevin: Tried rolling back GPU driver on a canary node to 451.67 — p99 improved but still > baseline. Suggests kernel change is primary, driver amplifies. Need bisect across kernel versions and vendor driver.

carlos: Also observed heavy writeback from our model checkpointing process that coincides with hourly snapshot job. That job was fine before but now I/O scheduling delays cause downstream request latency. We should schedule snapshot off-peak or use throttled IO for checkpoints.

anya: Action items I propose:
- rollback kernel on impacted Dedicated pool nodes to previous stable kernel (rollback plan ready).
- set temporary vm tunables (dirty_bytes -> 16MB, dirty_ratio -> 5) and nomerges until patch deployed.
- add IO cgroup limits for checkpointing to avoid saturating nvme.
- full bisect: kernel vs driver vs nvme firmware. assign to eng-infra + eng-runtime.
- Support to send customer repro steps and temporary mitigation steps.

support-bot: Case INC-2026-1304 created; customer notified with rollback/mitigation steps.

linda: Filed vendor ticket with NVMe driver vendor: VND-4451, attaching our iostat/dmesg and repro waveform. They acknowledged possible scheduler regression in kernel 5.16+ with certain nvme controllers.

kevin: Longer-term: add model-level response caching for short-term queries, plus route heavy checkpoint jobs to isolated maintenance windows. Also add an automatic guard that detects kernel-induced qdepth spikes and triggers rolling fallback to older kernel image.

anya: I'm going to coordinate the rollback on the impacted node pool now, will post timeline and links. cc @oncall-sre for pager handoff.

carlos: Thanks — please capture exact diff of kernel packages we pushed so we can pin in the release notes. Also schedule postmortem once we have root cause.

anya: Will do. Closing interim triage, keeping thread open for updates. :memo:
